newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian farmers block Milan roads over milk quota.
newsitem.headline: Italian farmers block Milan roads over milk quota.

text.p: Farmers brought new chaos to Italy's second city Sunday, blocking roads to the main airport and soccer stadium in a fourth day of growing protests over European Union milk quotas.

Passengers were forced to walk for miles in heavy rain and snow to reach Milan's international airport while soccer fans heading for the San Siro stadium faced delays after farmers blocked a main access point to the ground.

"Farmers are ready to come from all over the north of Italy to demonstrate," said Alberto Oldani, a farm worker at the San Siro blockade. "Yesterday we shut down one area of the city, today two, tomorrow five or six," he added.

The farmers started their protest Thursday, descending on Italy's financial heartland with hundreds of tractors as part of an increasingly bitter battle with Prime Minister Romano Prodi's government over EU fines for milk overproduction.
Brussels has slapped 370 billion lire ($235 million) of fines on Italian farmers for exceeding their milk quotas in the 1995-96 season.
Dairy farmers want the state to pay the whole levy and say a draft law aimed at compensating them for the fines does not go far enough. They also demand that the EU quotas be raised.
The government has offered farmers cheap-rate loans but has refused to take responsibility for the fines. Negotiations between the two sides broke down on Saturday.

Farmers say they have fallen victim to tough EU quotas, introduced in the 1980s, which allow them to produce just 60 percent of Italy's milk needs. The rest of the milk is imported from other EU countries.

Farmers at Linate said they were considering blocking Milan's intercontinental airport, Malpensa. One airport official warned that unless the Linate blockade was lifted, they would run out of airplane fuel there on Monday.
